0.long_answer: De Barsy syndrome, also known as progeroid syndrome of De Barsy, is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by cutis laxa (loose skin), corneal clouding, skeletal abnormalities, and premature aging. Research has pointed to mutations in several genes involved in proline metabolism and cellular functions. In particular, mutations in the PYCR1 gene, which encodes the mitochondrial enzyme pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase 1, have been implicated in the condition. This enzyme plays a critical role in the synthesis of proline, and its deficiency disrupts normal tissue structure and function, leading to the clinical features observed. Although other genes such as ALDH18A1 and ATP6V0A2 have also been studied in similar cutis laxa syndromes, mutations in PYCR1 are most consistently associated with the progeroid syndrome characterized by cutis laxa and corneal clouding.
